key_insight: Nonnegativity adds a “positive scattering” constraint that makes sparse tensor decompositions identifiable beyond classical dimension-only conditions.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper test for when nonnegative tensor models are uniquely recoverable, which is useful for interpretable factorization in signal processing, imaging, and data compression.
method: Combine a positive scattering term with a Lovitz–Petrov-style dimension budget.
Prove a positive splitting inequality for irreducible exchanges of nonnegative rank-one tensors.
Use graph connectivity to characterize when scattering activates with costs 0, 1, or +∞.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sufficient thresholds of 2|S|-2 for minimality/nonnegative rank and 2|S|-1 for uniqueness, plus examples where Kruskal and Lovitz–Petrov fail even after reshaping.
watch_item: The criterion depends on an optimization over intermediate factor spaces, so computing the scattering term and verifying connectivity may be nontrivial in large instances.
paper_title: Identifiability of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions via Positive Scattering
